title: Bibliography
basis: Written on 2026-11-17 for a generated lookup page. The page is produced by _research/bib-tools/run.sh from every page's Sources and Evidence section; this spec fixes its units and their order, and render.py writes the prose of each unit. One spec paragraph per unit of the page; each group's entry list is one paragraph with form list; the two tables are recorded as the evidence of the paragraph that introduces them. Intent, acceptance criteria, thesis and role are copied unchanged from journal-spec.json; the three supporting claims are this spec's own. No count is fixed here: every count on the page is computed by the generator on each run.

know: Every public source the pages cite, listed once with a stable R-number, its publication date or 'n.d., accessed 2026-11', its evidence type, the claim it supports and the pages citing it, by topic and by chapter.

The three groups of source the chapters use (company, product and investor sources; standards, regulation and official documentation; research and practitioner sources) and the marks '(secondary source)' and '(evidence age: N years)'.
That the register is generated from the chapters' Sources and Evidence sections, so an R-number identifies a source and does not rank it.
believe: A claim is as trustworthy as the kind and age of its source: a regulation records a requirement, audited accounts record reported numbers, an annual letter what a private company chose to say, documentation an interface as read on a date, an engineering post what a company said it had built that year.
can_do: Trace a figure or a statement in a chapter to its dated source and weigh it by evidence type and date.
Tell from an entry whether a statement about a provider's internals rests on current documentation or on an old engineering post.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader traces a claim to its entry and reads from the entry what kind of evidence it is, how old it is and which pages rely on it.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Using only this page: the idempotency chapter says a Stripe API v1 idempotency key and its stored response are kept for at least 24 hours. Find the entry behind that statement. What kind of source is it, what is its date, and what does the page tell you about how many other pages rely on it?
acceptance_criteria.expected: One entry with an R-number for Stripe's API reference on idempotent requests; official product documentation; undated, marked 'n.d., accessed 2026-11', so the access month says when it was read; the entry lists the pages that cite it, idempotency-and-retries among them.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader weighs a source by its type and date.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Using only this page: one entry is a 2017 engineering post marked '(evidence age: 9 years)', one is a documentation page marked 'n.d.', and one is marked '(secondary source)'. How far should a reader trust each for a claim about a provider today, and does any source describe Larkfield?
acceptance_criteria.expected: The 2017 post records what the company said it had built in 2017; the current system may differ, and the citing chapter says whether current documentation confirms it. 'n.d.' means undated documentation, so the access month (November 2026) shows when it was read, and it may have changed since. A secondary source is trade press or analysis, used only to fill a gap and named as such in the sentence that cites it. No source describes Larkfield, which is fictional; labeled inferences, recommendations and assumptions are the author's.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader can say what is deliberately absent from the register.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Using only this page: is the Productscape planning model listed as a source for any claim, and where would you find the source for a statement the book marks 'Not public'?
acceptance_criteria.expected: The planning model is named once as planning material and supports no claim. A 'Not public' statement has no source by definition: it records that the public record searched up to the research cut-off of 17 November 2026 does not say.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the introduction alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first section heading) can predict what the page contains and the kind of material it uses.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the introduction: what will this page give you, in what order, and from what kind of material?
acceptance_criteria.expected: A register that traces each claim to its source and shows when that evidence was published or read, researched up to 17 November 2026, with 'n.d.' meaning undated; then how to read an entry (R-numbers identify and do not rank; evidence type; evidence age; secondary sources), a topic index, entries by topic and sources by chapter. Material: the chapters' own Sources and Evidence sections; the planning model is listed once as planning material, not evidence, and Larkfield has no sources.

thesis.question: Which sources does the book cite, and how much does each kind of source support?
thesis.claim: The book cites each public source once, under a stable R-number, with its date, its evidence type and the pages that rely on it, and the type and date decide how much the source supports: a regulation or a network rule supports a requirement, audited accounts support a reported figure, undated documentation supports an interface as read in November 2026, and an engineering post supports only what the company said it had built in the year of the post.
thesis.disputed_by: The view that a company's engineering blog is the best evidence of how its systems work regardless of when the post was written, so that a link in the chapter is enough and a register of types and dates adds nothing.
thesis.so_what: A reader who wants to rely on a statement about Stripe or Adyen looks up its entry first and, where the entry is an engineering post older than about three years or an undated page, checks the current documentation before building on it.
thesis.how_why: The register is generated from the chapters' Sources and Evidence sections, so it shows what the chapters do not show one at a time: how many pages lean on one source, and how old the evidence under a subject is. That matters in this book because the public material is uneven: Stripe's best-known posts on idempotency, rate limiting and versioning are from 2017, Adyen's account of its accounting design is from 2021, most documentation pages are undated, and Stripe's company figures come from annual letters while Adyen's come from audited reports.

supporting_claims.claim: Each public source the pages cite is listed once under a stable R-number that identifies and does not rank it, with its date or 'n.d.', its evidence type, the claim it supports and the pages that cite it.

The evidence type and the date of a source decide how much it supports, and the register shows both on every entry: the type in words, undated pages as 'n.d.', evidence from November 2023 or earlier with an age mark and second-hand evidence with a secondary mark.

Because it is generated from every page's Sources and Evidence section, the register shows what one chapter's list cannot: how many pages lean on one source, and how the kind and age of the evidence differ between Stripe, Adyen and the other publishers; an entry is found by publisher or by citing page.

role.contribution: Closes the book's apparatus: every cited source once, typed and dated, so any claim can be traced to a document by topic or by chapter and weighed by its age.

flow.rationale: How to read an entry comes first, because every entry is weighed by its type, date and marks, and the counts by publisher tell the reader what kind of evidence to expect before they meet nine hundred entries. The topic index then maps the publisher groups before the entries themselves. The by-chapter list reads the same sources from the citing side and comes last because a reader who starts from a chapter needs the R-numbers the groups define; the closing ends the reference pages. Grouping by publisher instead of by the book's parts follows from the thesis: who published a source and in what kind of document decides how much it supports, and one documentation page is cited from several parts.

hook.content: Use this register to trace a claim in any chapter to its public source and to see when that evidence was published or read.

bridge.from_reader_world: The reader has met a figure, a rule or a statement about Stripe or Adyen in a chapter, or a definition in the glossary that rests on a chapter, and wants to know what document stands behind it and how far to trust it.
bridge.to_topic: Every cited source is gathered here once, typed and dated, by publisher and by chapter.

conclusion.heading: Sources by Chapter
conclusion.synthesis: The four pages answer the four lookups a chapter leaves the reader with (where, which record, what word, what source), and each answer points back to the chapter that owns it. Together they also draw the book's outer line: a planning model that is not evidence, cards filled with fiction, definitions that defer to chapters, and a register in which a claim about a provider ends at a dated document or does not appear.
conclusion.so_what: A claim, a term or a card in any chapter can be checked against its owning chapter and its dated source without rereading the book, and a disagreement between them is a defect to fix.

callback.to: This page's KEY POINTS: the type and the date decide how much a source supports; look the entry up before relying on a statement about Stripe or Adyen.
callback.how: The closing turns them into the course of action for using the whole book and, as the Reference part's closing, names the four lookups the four reference pages answer.

takeaway.content: Before relying on a statement about Stripe or Adyen from this book, find its source in the register, check the source's type and date, and keep documented facts, labeled inferences and Larkfield apart.

transition_in.introduces: The same sources read from each citing page.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Each citing page, in reading order, with the number of sources it cites and their R-numbers in identifier order; pages that cite nothing of their own are omitted.
No source describes Larkfield, which is fictional, and the recommendations, labeled inferences and labeled assumptions are the author's judgement.

transition_in.introduces: What no source stands behind.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The four reference pages answer four lookups that point back to the owning chapter, so before building on a statement about Stripe or Adyen the reader finds its entry, reads its type and date and checks current documentation where the entry is old or undated.

transition_in.introduces: The close of the reference pages.

Definitions of terms and the Stripe and Adyen vocabulary crosswalk

open_questions: Four pages were still being written or verified when the register was first generated on 2026-11-17 (stripe-and-adyen-bets-compared, toolkit, domain-coverage, glossary); rerun run.sh when they are final and read the audit lines.
Mastercard's rule documents could not be retrieved (HTTP 403), so no Mastercard rule is cited from Mastercard's own text; the register says so under the card networks group.

decision_log.decision: Entries are grouped by publisher (card networks and schemes; regulators, law and standards; Stripe in three groups; Adyen in three groups; other companies; research and practitioner sources; the planning model), not by the book's parts as in ORDERED.
rejected: Grouping by part: one documentation page is cited from several parts, and the thesis weighs a source by who published it and in what kind of document.

decision_log.decision: Eleven evidence types follow the thesis: regulation or regulator publication; standard, network rule or scheme publication; annual report, results or filing; annual letter; product and API documentation; terms, legal or licence page; engineering post or talk; press release or announcement; company guide, product page or blog; practitioner or secondary source; the author's planning model.
rejected: One type for all company material
Calling half-year letters and quarterly updates audited: only an annual report or a Form 10-K carries audited statements, and the table says so.

decision_log.decision: The age mark is computed from the entry's date against the cut-off of November 2026 and shown on every entry dated November 2023 or earlier; where a chapter wrote the mark itself its wording is kept ('evidence age: 11 years; in force').
rejected: Showing the mark only where a chapter wrote it, which would leave old sources unmarked when the citing chapter forgot.

decision_log.decision: A documentation page and its Markdown export, a stripe.com page with and without a default locale prefix, and a redirected address are one entry; country editions of pricing and legal pages stay separate entries because their content differs.

Where chapters gave one URL different dates or titles, the page was fetched and the chapters' Sources entries were corrected to agree (format only); the generator's overrides are kept for what cannot be fixed in a chapter.
rejected: Resolving conflicts only inside the generator, which would leave the chapters disagreeing.
